subject: generating PNGs on EC2 without a monitor

messages.author: d23df0a7a9d8566b
messages.subject: generating PNGs on EC2 without a monitor
parts:
Trying to set up a process to run some batch ggplots on an EC2 server in the cloud with no monitor.

Got most of the way there but get errors when alpha <1 .

Installed R from source using these helpful pointers (didn't see R binaries for Amazon's CentOS-like Linux distro) 
http://jeffreybreen.wordpress.com/2011/07/08/install-r-amazon-linux-ec2/

ran a script with a ggsave - didn't work because it needs an X server

> ggsave (ggpshade, filename="/var/R/temp/contrib2.png", width=8, height=6, dpi=72)
Error in X11(paste("png::", filename, sep = ""), width, height, pointsize,  :
  unable to start device PNG

Googled some more and launched Xvfb - 

sudo Xvfb :1 -screen 0 1280x1024x24 -fbdir /tmp -fp /usr/share/X11/fonts/misc -nolisten tcp -shmem &

export DISPLAY=:1

> ggsave (ggpshade, filename="/var/R/temp/contrib2.png", width=8, height=6, dpi=72)
Warning messages:
1: Stacking not well defined when ymin != 0
2: Stacking not well defined when ymin != 0
3: In grid.Call.graphics("L_rect", x$x, x$y, x$width, x$height, resolveHJust(x$just,  :
  semi-transparency is not supported on this device: reported only once per page

I have some bars with alpha=0.5, if I take those out it works without error. Not the end of the world but wanted to shade some periods and see the background major/minor tick grid . 

Tried setting higher bit depth, highest I could get with Xvfb was 24. Didn't see anything else applicable in Xvfb or Xserver manpage.

Any way to create PNGs or JPGs without running X? Any best practices for running graphics on headless compute servers? Maybe different X server, not X.org, or different virtual device, parameters? 

Any suggestions greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: generating PNGs on EC2 without a monitor
parts:
You could try,

- passing type = "cairo" to ggsave, see ?png

- using cairoDevice::cairo_png

- the Cairo package

HTH,

baptiste
